gist: Exploration and use of outer space, including the Moon and other celestial bodies, is for the benefit of all countries and is the province of all mankind; free access and freedom of scientific investigation.
Outer space and celestial bodies are not subject to national appropriation by claim of sovereignty, use, occupation or other means.
Activities are carried on in accordance with international law, including the UN Charter.

short: No weapons of mass destruction; peaceful celestial bodies
gist: No nuclear weapons or other WMD in orbit, on celestial bodies or stationed in space; the Moon and other celestial bodies used exclusively for peaceful purposes; no bases, weapons tests or manoeuvres there.
States render all possible assistance to astronauts in distress and return them; states report phenomena dangerous to astronauts.
States bear international responsibility for national activities in space, whether by government or non-governmental entities, which require authorization and continuing supervision.
A launching state is internationally liable for damage caused by its space objects.

short: Jurisdiction, control and return of objects
gist: The state of registry retains jurisdiction and control over objects and personnel; ownership is unaffected; found objects are returned.
Cooperation and mutual assistance; due regard for others' interests; avoid harmful contamination; consult before potentially harmful interference.
States consider requests to observe the flight of space objects launched by others, on equal terms.

short: Informing the UN and the public
gist: States inform the UN Secretary-General, the public and the scientific community of the nature, conduct, locations and results of their activities.
Stations, installations, equipment and vehicles on the Moon and celestial bodies are open to representatives of other parties on a basis of reciprocity.
The treaty applies whether activities are carried on by one state, jointly, or within international organizations.
Open to all states; enters into force on deposit of five ratifications including those of the three depositary governments (UK, USA, USSR).
Any party may propose amendments, which take effect for parties accepting them once a majority has accepted.
A party may withdraw by written notice, effective one year after notification.
English, Russian, French, Spanish and Chinese texts are equally authentic.
